$comment: Design tokens. Derived from design-brief.md §5 and §6. Owned by the project lead. Both board-render and visual-design read this; neither edits it. Values here are authoritative — an agent that needs a colour or a size not listed proposes an addition and stops.

$rules: coral is emphasis only, never error. Nothing in this product reads as an error.
A wrong or rejected action gets a gentle nudge in heeler, not a red alarm.
White and black pieces must differ in hue as well as lightness, so the distinction survives poor screens and colour vision differences.

body.$comment: Lexend was designed to improve reading performance in children. Do not substitute.

$rules: Sentence case everywhere. No all-caps labels.
Body text never smaller than 1rem. These are beginner readers.

touch.$comment: Roughly double the adult minimum. Ages 6-8 have developing fine motor control. This is a floor, not a target.

$rules: Motion answers an action. A piece moving, a node unlocking, a celebration firing.
No ambient motion, no scroll-triggered fades, no hover effects on everything.
prefers-reduced-motion must be respected. Reduce to instant, do not remove feedback.
Square colours derive from board.size. Never hardcode a grid.
Legal destinations on empty squares: a filled dot.
Legal destinations on capturable pieces: a ring around the square.
This affordance is the single most important teaching element in the product. It is never subtle.

quality.responsive: tablet and desktop equally; must not break on mobile
